title: iTunes/Finder error 4013
fullDescription:
Error 4013 (and the related 4005, 4014) appears in iTunes or Finder when the iPhone disconnects during a restore or update. The cause is usually a faulty USB cable, faulty USB port, or a hardware fault on the iPhone (NAND flash, baseband).

If the error persists across multiple cables and computers, the iPhone hardware likely needs service.

fixSteps.title: Use MFi cable and Apple computer port
fixSteps.instruction: Use Apple-certified Lightning cable and a direct USB port (not a hub) on a Mac if possible.

fixSteps.title: Force restart iPhone
fixSteps.instruction: iPhone 8+: Vol Up, Vol Down, hold Side until Apple logo. Older: Home + Side until logo.

fixSteps.title: Update iTunes/macOS, retry
fixSteps.instruction: Update iTunes (Win) or macOS (Mac) and retry the restore.

fixSteps.title: DFU mode restore
fixSteps.instruction: Put iPhone into DFU and try restore again from Finder/iTunes.

fixSteps.title: Apple service
fixSteps.instruction: If 4013 persists with multiple cables/computers, NAND or logic board service required.

whenToCallPro: If error persists after cable, port, and DFU restore.

faq.a: If hardware fault, possibly. Try iCloud/computer backup first.

title: iTunes/Finder error 4014
shortDescription: Connection lost during restore - hardware suspected.
fullDescription: Error 4014 closely related to 4013, indicates iTunes lost connection with the iPhone during restore. Usually pointing to a hardware issue with the iPhone (NAND flash chip).

fixSteps.title: Try different cable + USB port
fixSteps.instruction: Use MFi cable, plug into rear USB port on PC or directly to Mac.

fixSteps.title: DFU restore
fixSteps.instruction: Force into DFU mode and restore.

fixSteps.title: Apple service
fixSteps.instruction: Likely NAND failure — Apple Store / AASP.

faq.a: Very similar; both point to hardware.

title: iTunes/Finder error 4005
shortDescription: USB connection or hardware issue during restore.
fullDescription: Error 4005 appears when iPhone update/restore fails — usually due to USB connection issue or NAND flash issue. Diagnostic steps mirror 4013/4014.

title: iTunes error 9
shortDescription: Connection lost during restore - kernel panic.
fullDescription: Error 9 indicates the iPhone disconnected from the computer because of a kernel panic during restore. Often hardware-related (NAND, baseband) but can also be triggered by faulty USB cables or security software interference.

fixSteps.title: Disable antivirus/firewall
fixSteps.instruction: Temporarily disable to rule out interference.

fixSteps.title: Use MFi cable + USB 2.0 port
fixSteps.instruction: Plug into back USB 2.0 port (not 3.0 hub).

title: iTunes error 29
fullDescription: Error 29 typically appears on older iPhones (4S, 5) when the battery is not recognized as genuine. After third-party battery replacements, iTunes refuses to restore.

fixSteps.title: Replace with OEM battery
fixSteps.instruction: Replace battery with original Apple part or an authentic Texas Instruments cell.

fixSteps.title: Reseat battery flex
fixSteps.instruction: Open phone, ensure battery connector is fully seated.

whenToCallPro: If you don't want to open the phone.

faq.a: Newer phones show battery service warning instead of error 29.

title: iTunes error 1
fullDescription: Error 1 typically points to a baseband chip failure — the part of the iPhone responsible for cellular communication. Once it fails, iPhone may show 'No Service' permanently and refuses to restore.

fixSteps.title: DFU restore attempt
fixSteps.instruction: Try DFU mode restore via Mac/PC.

fixSteps.title: Board-level repair
fixSteps.instruction: Microsoldering shop can replace baseband — specialized service.

faq.a: Apple typically swaps the whole device.

title: iTunes error 1110
shortDescription: Restore failed - logic board issue suspected.
fullDescription: Error 1110 appears during iPhone restore and is typically associated with logic board issues. Less common than 4013/4014 but indicates similar hardware failure.

fixSteps.title: DFU restore
fixSteps.instruction: Force DFU mode and try restore.

title: iTunes error 1109
fullDescription: Error 1109 appears when iTunes/Finder cannot validate the firmware signature with Apple servers, often during attempts to install older iOS versions Apple no longer signs.

fixSteps.title: Use signed iOS version
fixSteps.instruction: Check ipsw.me for currently signed iOS versions for your device.

faq.a: Only to versions Apple still signs.

title: iTunes error 10
shortDescription: LLB (Low Level Bootloader) missing in IPSW.
fullDescription: Error 10 appears during iPhone restore when iOS firmware lacks the LLB component required by the device, or there's a logic board issue (often after motherboard repair).

fixSteps.title: Re-download IPSW
fixSteps.instruction: Delete cached IPSW (Mac: ~/Library/iTunes/iPhone Software Updates/), let iTunes redownload.

title: iTunes error 14
shortDescription: USB connection broken during firmware extraction.
fullDescription: Error 14 appears when iTunes/Finder fails to write the firmware to the iPhone, typically due to broken USB connection mid-restore. Sometimes related to corrupted IPSW file.

fixSteps.title: Re-download IPSW
fixSteps.instruction: Hold Option (Mac) or Shift (Win) and Restore to manually select fresh IPSW.

title: iTunes error 26
fullDescription: Error 26 appears when iTunes cannot flash the NOR partition containing critical iOS files. Often hardware-related (NOR flash chip) or wrong IPSW.

fixSteps.title: Verify IPSW model
fixSteps.instruction: Make sure IPSW matches device exactly (e.g., iPhone 13,2 vs 13,3).

title: iTunes error 28
shortDescription: Hardware error - dock connector or USB controller.
fullDescription: Error 28 indicates a hardware-level problem with the iPhone, often the Lightning/USB-C connector itself or the device's USB controller chip on the logic board.

fixSteps.title: Clean Lightning port
fixSteps.instruction: Use wooden toothpick to gently remove lint and debris.

faq.a: Yes, pocket lint is the #1 cause of port issues.

title: iTunes error 53
fullDescription: Error 53 historically appeared on iPhones with Touch ID where the home button had been replaced by a third party. Apple released a fix in iOS 9.2.1 but related security validation issues persist on Face ID models when components are swapped.

causes.cause: Third-party Touch ID home button replacement

fixSteps.title: Update iOS
fixSteps.instruction: Apple's iOS 9.2.1+ includes recovery for error 53.

fixSteps.title: Restore original home button
fixSteps.instruction: Reinstall original Touch ID home button if available.

faq.a: After third-party home button replacement, Touch ID won't pair without Apple.

title: iTunes error 1015
fullDescription: Error 1015 typically appears when attempting to install an iOS version older than what's currently on the device, or after using third-party tools to modify the system.

fixSteps.title: Use signed iOS
fixSteps.instruction: Only restore to currently-signed iOS for your device.

fixSteps.title: DFU restore
fixSteps.instruction: Force DFU then restore latest signed iOS.

faq.a: Apple stops signing old iOS to push security.

title: No Service / Searching
fullDescription: iPhone shows No Service or stuck on Searching when the cellular modem cannot connect to towers. Possible causes range from carrier outage to SIM issue to baseband failure.

fixSteps.title: Toggle Airplane mode
fixSteps.instruction: Enable Airplane mode for 30 seconds, disable.

fixSteps.title: Reset Network Settings
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset > Reset > Reset Network Settings.

fixSteps.title: Reseat SIM / contact carrier
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and reinsert SIM. Verify line is active.

fixSteps.title: Apple service for hardware
fixSteps.instruction: If software fixes fail, baseband/antenna repair needed.

faq.a: Sometimes carrier settings update fixes it.
